tests.name: two synthetic atomic writers preserve both increments in ten sampled rounds
stale synthetic legacy-style write can erase an atomic writer action
lock-aware contender waits and then acquires after release
uncooperative synthetic writer modifies IndexedDB while Web Lock is held
v2 waits for open v1 connection and keeps synthetic value
explicit synthetic v1 reopen after v2 returns VersionError
separate synthetic database names allow v1 and v2 opens
same final pair can come from two increments or one copied increment

limitations: Synthetic miniature IndexedDB and Web Locks clients only: not the real +14 application, new application, Hive or the user diary.
Fresh non-persistent Playwright context on a random loopback origin inside a network namespace; no cloud, accounts or real data.
Only selected schedules were tested. No crash, power loss, real offline mode, Safari/iOS, Android, multi-device, Auth, sync, migration or backup/restore.
Atomic transactions and separate databases are demonstrations, not a proposed production patch or proof of a safe rollback or merge.
Two final values alone do not encode whether they arose from one copied operation or two independent operations; additional trusted provenance could change what is knowable.
